issues.t: Hard to refuel: hydrogen stations closed, broken or out of fuel
issues.sym: You can't find a working hydrogen station nearby, stations are closed for repair or out of hydrogen, pumps won't take payment or stop mid-fill, and there can be long lines. Some owners have run out of fuel and needed a tow.
issues.why: The Mirai can only refuel at hydrogen stations, and there are few of them, almost all in California. Supply shortages and station breakdowns have hit owners hard, and Mirai owners have sued Toyota over it.
issues.next: Check a live station-status app before every trip and don't let the tank run low. Keep a backup plan for longer drives. If you're thinking of buying one, make sure a reliable station is close to home and work.

issues.sym: A message says "FC malfunction, return vehicle to dealer for service," and code P1DEF (fuel cell stack performance) is stored. Power may be reduced.
issues.why: The fuel control module's settings could flag the fuel cell stack as underperforming. Toyota revised the fuel control module calibration in a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer certified for fuel cell vehicles check it. Ask whether the calibration update is covered for your car: that depends on the exact fault, the date the car first went into service and its mileage. Key fuel cell parts carry an 8-year/100,000-mile warranty from the in-service date.

issues.t: Fueling problems from a lost nozzle O-ring
issues.sym: The car won't fill properly or the fill stops early, and the station may show a fueling fault. The rubber O-ring on the car's hydrogen fill port can come off during fueling.
issues.why: Toyota found that some fueling sessions could pull off the 35 MPa O-ring on the Mirai's hydrogen receptacle, which affects the seal with the station nozzle.
issues.next: If fills keep failing at more than one station, have a Toyota fuel cell dealer inspect the fill receptacle and O-ring.

issues.t: Chirping noise from the rear at certain speeds
issues.sym: A high-pitched chirp from the back of the car that shows up only at certain speeds.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin (T-SB-0286-17) for this rear chirp noise on some 2016-2017 cars, filed under the fuel system.
issues.next: Point out the noise and the speed it happens at to a Toyota dealer and ask about bulletin T-SB-0286-17.

issues.sym: One or both front seat heaters don't warm up, and a light on the A/C control panel may not come on.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for an inoperative seat heater and an unlit A/C panel indicator on these cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the seat heater and panel against bulletin T-SB-0041-18.

issues.t: Safety Connect may send the wrong location
issues.sym: No obvious symptom, but if you use emergency assistance or crash notification, the system may report the wrong location.
issues.why: A programming error in the data communication module made it miscalculate GPS position after November 2, 2019. Toyota fixed it under limited service campaign K0P.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check whether campaign K0P has been done on your VIN.

issues.t: Debris from the hydrogen tank end protector
issues.sym: No symptoms while driving. Bits of debris are found on the underbody cover near the end of the hydrogen tank during service.
issues.why: Toyota traced the debris to the protective cap on the end of the hydrogen tank.
issues.next: Have a Toyota fuel cell dealer inspect the tank area at your next service. Hydrogen tanks should only be handled by trained technicians.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates with nothing ahead
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own with no car or object in front and no warning first, which can startle you or cause a rear-end crash.
issues.why: Owners report false triggers of the pre-collision braking system; the dealer could not find a fault in at least one case.
issues.next: Report each event to the dealer and to NHTSA. Keep the front radar and camera area clean, and ask the dealer to check sensor aim and software.

issues.t: Pre-collision braking or warnings act up
issues.sym: The automatic emergency braking or forward collision warning goes off when nothing is there, or doesn't act as expected, sometimes leading to crashes.
issues.why: Owners filed several NHTSA complaints about the forward collision avoidance system on 2022-2023 Mirais, including some that involved crashes. No single cause has been published.
issues.next: Report every event to a Toyota dealer and NHTSA. Ask the dealer to check for software updates and sensor calibration.

issues.t: Navigation maps out of date or won't update
issues.sym: The navigation maps are old, or a map or software update fails.
issues.why: Cars with Premium Audio with Dynamic Navigation need a special Toyota USB service tool for map and software updates, so they often go without them.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to install the latest map and head unit software.

issues.sym: The car won't power on or shows electrical warnings after sitting for a while, especially if not driven daily.
issues.why: Like other electrified Toyotas, the Mirai relies on a small 12-volt battery to start up its systems. Sitting, heat, cold and small electrical drains run it down, and Toyota has bulletins on 12-volt battery care.
issues.next: Drive the car regularly or use a battery maintainer if it will sit. Have the 12-volt battery tested if you see repeated low-voltage warnings.

issues.t: Check engine light from stuck fuel cell air valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes P1F6C71 (air sealing valve actuator stuck) or P1F6E71 (air pressure regulating valve actuator stuck).
issues.why: The valves that control air flow to the fuel cell stack can be flagged as stuck. Toyota modified the EV control computer logic to make this less likely.
issues.next: Have a Toyota fuel cell dealer read the codes and apply the EV control computer update from bulletin T-SB-0043-23.

issues.sym: A "FCV system malfunction" warning appears on the dash even though the car seems to drive normally.
issues.why: Improper programming of the EV control computer could trigger a false warning. Toyota fixed it with a software update under campaign 22TD01.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether campaign 22TD01 or a later EV control software update has been done on your car.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power with the screen going black
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive power, and the center display may go black and reboot. Owners describe it happening at low speed and on the freeway.
issues.why: NHTSA complaints describe sudden power loss without warning lights. The cause hasn't been confirmed, and dealers could not always reproduce it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get to a safe spot and restart the car. Report it to a Toyota fuel cell dealer and NHTSA right away, and ask the dealer to save stored codes.

issues.t: Rear suspension creaks or clicks over bumps
issues.sym: A creak or click from under the rear of the car when braking or driving over bumps.
issues.why: Toyota traced the noise to the rear suspension member (subframe) and issued a bulletin with a repair.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check for bulletin T-SB-0047-23. It is usually covered under warranty.

issues.t: Stability control may stay off after restart (recall)
issues.sym: The stability control (VSC) may not turn back on when you restart the car, and the VSC off light may stay lit.
issues.why: A software error in the skid control computer can leave stability control off after a restart.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the skid control software for free.

issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the backup camera picture takes a couple of seconds to appear.
issues.why: The parking assist computer software was programmed incorrectly, delaying the rearview image.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the parking assist software for free.

issues.t: Backup camera can freeze or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: In reverse, the backup camera image can freeze or the screen can go blank on cars with the 360-degree Panoramic View Monitor.
issues.why: A software error in the parking assist system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the parking assist software for free.
